stories.headline: 100 million African children are not in school: What’s driving the trend and how to reverse it
stories.summary: More than 100 million children and adolescents in Africa remain out of school, despite many countries adopting universal basic education policies. The total potential population of children and adolescents is 469 million. After years of progress, the situation is deteriorating, with recent data showing a decline. In 2000, over 100 million children were out-of-school in primary, lower secondary, and upper secondary levels. The African Union Commission and UNESCO have committed to reducing the out-of-school population by 58 million by 2030. Currently, the trend is a concern, with millions of children at risk of not returning to school. The numbers indicate a need for renewed efforts to improve education access and attainment across the continent, particularly in primary, lower secondary, and upper secondary levels.

stories.headline: China-US: Trump sees a 'fantastic future' between the two countries
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, predicting a "fantastic future together" for the two countries. The high-stakes meeting aimed to address thorny issues including trade disputes, Taiwan tensions, and Iran. Trump expressed respect for China and its achievements, stating that the relationship between China and the US would be "better than ever before." The US described the meeting as "highly productive," while Trump called it "the biggest summit ever." China seeks to leverage its domestic market and rare earth supply chain dominance to gain US opposition to Taiwan independence and reduced restrictions on high-end tech. The meeting's outcome is expected to have significant implications for the future of US-China relations and global trade. Trump's optimistic tone suggests a potential shift in the countries' diplomatic stance.

stories.headline: Cuba has run out of diesel and oil, energy minister says
stories.summary: Cuba's energy minister, Vicente de la O Levy, has announced that the country has completely run out of diesel and fuel oil. The shortage has led to the worst rolling blackouts in decades, with scattered protests breaking out in Havana. The US blockade, which was tightened after the Trump administration declared Cuba a threat to national security, has severely limited the island's access to fuel. The situation was further exacerbated by the US attack on Venezuela, Cuba's oil-rich ally, in January. As a result, Cuba is facing a severe energy crisis, with Minister de la O Levy stating that "we have absolutely no diesel." The fuel shortage has sparked unrest, with protests reported in the capital city, highlighting the dire situation facing the communist-run island.

stories.headline: US aid cuts leave Somalia struggling during another deadly drought
stories.summary: Somalia is experiencing a deadly drought, considered one of the worst in its history, with dry rivers and withered crops. The crisis is exacerbated by aid cuts, particularly from the US, which had been the country's top donor. Aid funding to Somalia decreased to $531 million in 2025, down from nearly five times that amount in 2022. The US aid cuts, initiated by the Trump administration, have severely impacted the country. Somalia's reliance on imported food and fuel, mostly from the Middle East, has also been affected by the Iran war, leading to rising prices. The humanitarian funding shortfall has left hundreds of thousands without access to safe water, increasing the risk of disease outbreaks and pushing many Somalis into hunger.

stories.headline: Meta launches WhatsApp ’incognito’ mode to address privacy concerns for AI chats
stories.summary: Meta has launched an "Incognito Chat" mode for Meta AI on WhatsApp, addressing privacy concerns for AI chats. This mode allows users to have private, temporary conversations with Meta's artificial intelligence assistant. Once enabled, conversations with Meta AI will not be stored, providing a way to have chat history-free discussions. The feature is similar to Incognito Mode in Google Chrome or Private Browsing in Safari. The launch aims to address concerns that Meta's AI assistant could read and store user conversations. With Incognito Chat, users can expect no chat history to be stored, providing a more private experience when interacting with Meta AI on WhatsApp and the Meta AI app. This update is part of Meta's efforts to enhance user privacy and security when using its AI-powered chat services.

stories.headline: Instagram introduces ‘Instants’ for disappearing photo sharing
stories.summary: Instagram has introduced "Instants," a feature for disappearing photo sharing. The feature allows users to share unedited, spontaneous photos with their close friends or mutual followers that can be viewed only once. Instants disappear once they've been seen and cannot be screenshotted. They also expire after 24 hours. Users can add captions to their Instants, but editing is not allowed. The feature is now live globally, accessible from the bottom right corner of a user's Instagram profile. Instants were previously tested in Spain and Italy before being rolled out to select users and eventually all users worldwide on Wednesday. The new feature is part of Instagram's efforts to enhance user experience and provide more sharing options.

stories.headline: A legacy in blue: Seiko marks 145 years with a striking new limited edition Astron GPS solar
stories.summary: Seiko marks its 145th anniversary with a limited-edition Astron GPS Solar watch, featuring a titanium 43.4mm case and light silver geometric dial with striking blue accents. The timepiece is powered by the new GPS Solar Dual Time Chronograph Caliber 5X63 movement, offering dual-time GPS syncing and a Quick-Change band system. This new creation joins the Seiko Astron collection, which has a legacy dating back to 1969 when the original Seiko Astron was released as the world's first commercial quartz watch. The limited-edition watch commemorates Seiko's milestone anniversary, building on the brand's reputation for innovative watchmaking. The Astron GPS Solar is driven by efficient GPS solar technology, providing essential features for travelers, including automatic GPS time and timezone adjustment. The watch's design and functionality pay tribute to Seiko's heritage and commitment to precision timekeeping.

stories.headline: Battlefield 6's New Map Fixes One of the Game's Biggest Issues
stories.summary: Battlefield 6 has received a new map, Railway to Golmud, a remake of a Battlefield 4 classic, which addresses one of the game's biggest issues: a lack of airspace. The large map provides ample space for pilots, improving gameplay. This update follows previous patches that aimed to fix balance, flow, and gameplay issues after player backlash. Developer DICE had acknowledged the "burning issues" and committed to addressing them quickly. The latest update is part of the game's ongoing overhaul, with previous patches released to kick off the next stage of Season 1. The game's creative leads have been working to resolve player concerns, with a large corrective patch prepared to address major issues. The updates demonstrate the developer's efforts to improve the game and enhance player experience.

stories.headline: Rory McIlroy fit to step up in quest for seventh Major
stories.summary: Rory McIlroy is fit to compete in the US PGA Championship, seeking his seventh Major title. A two-time winner of the PGA Championship, McIlroy aims to win back-to-back Majors, which would tie him with Harry Vardon for the most Major wins by a European. McIlroy recently recovered from a back injury that affected his performance at the Players Championship, where he ended round one seven shots off the pace. Despite feeling "rusty," McIlroy is ready to challenge for more major glory at Aronimink in Newtown, Pennsylvania. He has been preparing for the course's difficult greens and wide landing areas, adopting a strategy of using his driver to bash the ball down the fairway and then figuring out his next move. McIlroy's experience and skill make him a strong contender for the championship.

stories.headline: Liverpool have endured a difficult title defence under Arne Slot as this Premier League season comes to a close
stories.summary: Liverpool's title defence under manager Arne Slot has been disappointing as the Premier League season comes to a close. Slot won the league in his first season, but the team's performance has been underwhelming in their title defence. Despite initial optimism, Liverpool suffered a dismal defeat at Manchester City, ending their title defence. The team's struggles have raised questions about Slot's future, with some speculating about his potential departure. Earlier in the season, there were concerns that Liverpool could finish in the bottom half of the table, but Slot had expressed confidence in the team's future. Now, with the season nearing its end, Slot faces difficult decisions to turn the team's fortunes around and restore success. The manager's next steps will be crucial in determining the team's trajectory.

stories.headline: Auckland rugby league player Eugene Hanna dies after injury in club's first game of season
stories.summary: Eugene Hanna, a 30-year-old rugby league player from Auckland, New Zealand, died on May 12 after sustaining an injury during a game. He played for the Glenora Bears' Premier Reserves squad in their season opener against the Te Atatū Roosters on May 2. The injury occurred during this match, and Hanna passed away 10 days later. The Glenora Rugby League Football Club confirmed his death in a Facebook post, with chair Jane Hunt expressing the club's condolences. Hanna's death is a tragic incident in the rugby league community, highlighting the risks and consequences of injuries in the sport. The incident has been reported as a fatal injury sustained during a match, adding to the list of professional rugby league players who have died due to injuries received during games.

stories.headline: Varsho's walk-off grand slam gives Blue Jays much-needed win
stories.summary: Daulton Varsho hit a walk-off grand slam in the 10th inning to give the Toronto Blue Jays a 5-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday. The game was played at Rogers Centre in Toronto. Varsho's grand slam came after a closely contested match, with the Blue Jays ultimately emerging victorious. Dylan Cease had a strong outing, striking out nine and allowing one run over seven innings. The win was a much-needed one for the Blue Jays, and Varsho's walk-off grand slam provided an exciting finish to the game. The grand slam was hit in the bottom of the 10th inning, securing the Blue Jays' win over the Rays. The victory came on May 13, 2026, at Rogers Centre in Toronto.

stories.headline: Woman gang-raped in sleeper bus in New Delhi A woman was gang-raped in a New Delhi sleeper bus; two suspects arrested and investigation underway.
stories.summary: A woman was gang-raped in a New Delhi sleeper bus on the night of May 11. The incident occurred inside a stationary bus, and the two accused, the driver and conductor, have been arrested. According to police sources, the incident was reported on May 12, and an investigation is underway. The Delhi Police has not yet issued an official statement on the incident. The opposition AAP has linked the incident to the 2012 Nirbhaya gangrape-murder case, drawing parallels between the two crimes. The arrests were made in connection with the incident, and further details are awaited as the investigation continues. The incident has sparked concern and outrage, with the opposition party criticizing the handling of the case.

stories.headline: Manipur police arrest six militants after murder of three Kuki-Zo church leaders Security personnel apprehended the self-styled “founder chairman” of the Kangleipak Communist Party - People’s War Group (KCP-PWG) along with four active cadres
stories.summary: Manipur police have arrested six militants, including the self-styled "founder chairman" of the Kangleipak Communist Party - People's War Group (KCP-PWG), in connection with the murder of three Kuki-Zo church leaders. The arrests were made after security personnel launched search operations in vulnerable areas. Additionally, three militants involved in extortion activities were apprehended, including one cadre from the Kangleipak Communist Party in Imphal West district. The arrests come amid ongoing tensions in the region, with three Kuki-Zo legislators being replaced as chairpersons of assembly committees without reason. The replacements include an MLA from the Naga People's Front. The security forces continue to conduct search operations to maintain law and order in the conflict-scarred state. The situation remains volatile, with authorities working to prevent further violence and instability.

stories.headline: Delhi horror: Woman alleges gangrape in private bus, 2 arrested NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have registered a case after a woman alleged that she was gang-raped in a private bus, officials said on Thursday.
stories.summary: Delhi Police have registered a case after a 30-year-old woman alleged she was gang-raped in a private bus in the capital. The incident occurred on Monday night in Delhi's Rani Bagh area, near Saraswati Vihar. The woman, a resident of a slum cluster in Pitampura, stated that the bus driver and conductor raped her inside the bus. An FIR was registered after her medical examination, and her statement was recorded by police. The bus has been seized, and both accused, the driver and conductor, have been arrested and are currently in custody. An investigation into the matter has been launched, with procedural formalities completed before the arrests were made. The case is currently underway, with police looking into the details of the incident.

stories.headline: Social media influencer 'The Skin Doctor' arrested by Delhi police The accused has been identified as Dr Neelam Singh, who describes himself as a “dermatologist speaking on social issues” on Youtube.
stories.summary: Dr. Neelam Singh, a social media influencer known as 'The Skin Doctor', was arrested by Delhi Police for allegedly posting objectionable tweets against the Kapur family. The tweets questioned the circumstances of businessman Sunjay Kapur's death and his will. Dr. Singh, a dermatologist, describes himself as a "dermatologist speaking on social issues" on Youtube. He was arrested following a complaint from the Kapur family, but was later granted bail. His lawyer, senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani, asserted that the case lacked legal grounds. Dr. Singh was released on bail a few hours after his arrest. The incident highlights the legal consequences of posting sensitive content on social media, particularly when it involves high-profile individuals and families. The case is ongoing, with further developments expected.

stories.headline: Jaishankar holds talks with Russia's Lavrov; trade, geopolitics top agenda
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held "productive" talks in New Delhi to advance bilateral cooperation in energy and trade. The discussions focused on energy cooperation, Brics coordination, and rising tensions in West Asia. The meeting reaffirmed the continuity of the India-Russia "Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership" amid shifting global alignments and mounting geopolitical pressure. Jaishankar and Lavrov's talks aimed to strengthen trade and geopolitical ties between the two nations. The meeting comes amid changing global dynamics, with India and Russia seeking to deepen their cooperation in key areas. The talks were described as wide-ranging and productive, with both sides committed to advancing their strategic partnership. The meeting highlighted the importance of the India-Russia relationship in the current geopolitical landscape.

stories.headline: Tim Cook's Next Act: Apple's Diplomat-In-Chief Tim Cook’s shift to Executive Chairman recasts him as Apple’s global diplomat, steering geopolitics while new CEO John Ternus drives innovation in a pivotal era
stories.summary: Tim Cook will transition to Executive Chairman of Apple's board of directors later this year, with John Ternus taking over as CEO. In his new role, Cook will focus on geopolitics and working with global policymakers, effectively becoming Apple's "Diplomat-in-Chief." This shift is expected to yield geopolitical wins for the company. Cook has been with Apple since 1998, serving as CEO since 2011, and has driven innovation and accessibility efforts. As Executive Chairman, he will assist with various parts of the company, leveraging his experience to shape Apple's future. The transition marks a pivotal era for the company, with Ternus driving innovation and Cook steering global relations. Cook's new role will involve working closely with policymakers, building on his existing relationships, including his past meetings with President Trump at the White House.

stories.headline: Fuel security cannot wait any longer It is time to start building an energy system that serves us and does not enslave us to geopolitics
stories.summary: The European Union is seeking to ensure a secure, affordable, and sustainable energy future amidst growing threats such as cyberattacks, supply disruptions, and extreme weather events. The Strait of Hormuz has been a focal point of concern, with the US attempting to convince China not to block a UN Security Council resolution condemning Iran's attacks on ships transiting the strait. Russia had previously vetoed an earlier proposal. The EU's energy security is heavily reliant on external factors, making it vulnerable to geopolitical tensions. To mitigate this, there is a need to create a more resilient energy system that is less dependent on external influences. The EU must consider alternative energy sources and strategies to reduce its vulnerability to supply disruptions and geopolitical instability. A secure energy future is crucial for Europe's economy and daily life.

stories.headline: From gold to large caps: Where PL Wealth sees opportunities for investors PL Capital says India equities face near term volatility from oil, inflation and geopolitics, but domestic liquidity, cyclicals and quality large caps support a
stories.summary: PL Capital warns of near-term volatility in India equities due to oil, inflation, and geopolitics. However, the firm remains optimistic about the long-term outlook, citing domestic liquidity, cyclicals, and quality large caps as supportive factors. PL Wealth identifies opportunities for investors in various assets, including gold and large caps. The firm's analysis suggests that certain battered large caps are poised to break out, presenting potential investment opportunities. Meanwhile, gold rates in India are updated daily to help investors make informed decisions. The latest gold rates and trends are sourced from trusted sources, providing investors with timely and reliable information to guide their investment choices. Overall, PL Capital's outlook emphasizes the importance of a long-term perspective and selective investment in quality assets amidst near-term volatility.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today Highlights: Sensex gains 789 pts, Nifty ends at 23,689 as US-China trade talks lift investor sentiment
stories.summary: The Indian stock market rose on Thursday, with the Sensex gaining 789 points to close at a higher level, and the Nifty ending at 23,689. The surge was driven by positive global market trends and optimism surrounding the ongoing US-China trade talks. Value buying and easing volatility also supported the gains. However, the progress was limited due to delays in the US-India trade deal. Earlier in the day, the BSE Sensex had added 281 points, and at one point was trading at 81,413.30, up 0.09 per cent. The gains indicate a lift in investor sentiment, despite previous sessions seeing losses due to the US-Iran conflict, which had caused the Sensex and Nifty 50 to fall over 0.6% each. The market's positive performance was a significant rebound from the previous day's losses.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Dalal Street Wakes Up and Chooses Green! Sensex Jumps Over 350 Points, Nifty Gains as Optimism Builds Ahead
stories.summary: The Indian benchmark indices gained on Thursday, with the Sensex rising 789 points to 75,398 and the Nifty jumping 277 points to 23,689. Top gainers included Bharti Airtel, HDFC Bank, Adani Ports, and Sun Pharmaceuticals. Earlier, on Tuesday, the Sensex ended trade 360 points higher at 83,899.78, and the Nifty closed at 25,700, up 131 points. The market rebounded after two days of decline, driven by easing crude oil prices, positive global cues, and sustained domestic buying. The gains came as election results were being declared for four states and one union territory, and after a panic-driven selloff and global jitters began to cool. The Sensex has since jumped over 350 points, with the Nifty also gaining, as optimism builds in the market.

stories.headline: Stock Market Opens Higher: Sensex Jumps Over 350 Points, Nifty Crosses 23,500 In early trading, GIFT Nifty is up 126 points, suggesting a strong start for benchmark indices following a positive close.
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices opened higher on Thursday, with the Sensex jumping over 350 points and the Nifty crossing 23,500. The GIFT Nifty was up 126 points, indicating a strong start for the market. Pharma and metal stocks led sectoral gains, while IT stocks declined, capping broader market gains. The Sensex gained 351 points to trade at a higher level, and the Nifty hit 23,570 in early trade. The positive start follows a mixed close on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached record highs, while the Dow lagged. The Indian market's gains were driven by metal and pharma stocks, with the Nifty trading above 23,550. The market opened firm, with the GIFT Nifty up 84 points, or 0.36 percent, around 9:10 am.

stories.headline: Sensex Today | Nifty 50 Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates: Sensex Gains 260 Points, Nifty Tops 23,500 At Opening Bell Amid Broad-Based Buying On Dalal Street
stories.summary: The Sensex gained 260 points, while the Nifty 50 topped 23,500 at the opening bell, driven by broad-based buying on Dalal Street. The Indian stock market witnessed a positive start, with the Sensex and Nifty experiencing significant gains. The market mood is upbeat, with real-time insights indicating a strong start to the day. The latest share market live updates show the NSE and BSE indices performing well, with top gainers and losers being tracked in real-time. Forex and commodity market news are also being closely monitored, with investors using the best trading platforms to make informed decisions. The share market today is being driven by various factors, including IPO news and FII/DII activity, with market news and headlines being updated regularly.

stories.headline: Apex Mining bucks lower output with 94% profit rise Apex Mining, led by Enrique Razon, posted a 94% surge in Q1 net income to P2.82 billion despite lower gold output and sales, as record gold prices and ongoing
stories.summary: Apex Mining, led by Enrique Razon, reported a 94% increase in Q1 net income to P2.82 billion, despite lower gold output and sales. The surge was driven by record gold prices. In the third quarter of 2024, the company posted a consolidated income of P1.31 billion, with higher tonnes milled and a surge in realized gold price being the main drivers. Previously, Apex Mining recorded a 9.1% year-on-year increase in its second-quarter net income to P210.05 million, attributed to higher metal prices. The company also saw a 17% increase in consolidated gross revenues for the first nine months, with a 14% rise in net income to Php 129.6 million in the third quarter compared to the same period in 2022. The strong performance was largely due to favorable gold prices.

stories.headline: Sensex down 500 pts from day's high, Nifty below 23,450: 6 key reasons behind market paring gains Sensex, Nifty declined from intraday highs amid profit booking, while a record low rupee also weighed on investor sentiment.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant downturn, with the Sensex falling 500 points from its day's high and the Nifty dropping below 23,450. The decline was driven by profit booking and a record low rupee, which weighed on investor sentiment. Over the past six sessions, the Sensex had gained 2.2% and the Nifty rose 2.4%, but this bullish sentiment appears to be taking a breather. Soaring oil prices and other factors also negatively impacted investor sentiment. Additionally, investors are awaiting US Fed Chair Jerome Powell's speech, which may provide commentary on the future interest rate trajectory after the Fed kept the benchmark rate unchanged. The market's decline reflects a cautious undertone in sentiment, with short-term traders booking profits in the absence of fresh positive triggers. The combination of these factors led to a decline of over 0.7% in both the Sensex and Nifty.

stories.headline: Rupee inches towards 96: Currency touches record low at 95.85 against US dollar India Business News: Rupee continued to tumble on Thursday, slumping 0.1% paise to 95.85 against US dollar in early trade.
stories.summary: The Indian rupee continued to decline, reaching a record low of 95.85 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday. This represents a 0.1% decrease. The currency has been consistently dragged down by rising crude oil prices and the ongoing Middle East conflict. The rupee has fallen 1.4% this week, with significant declines on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. On Tuesday, it dropped 40 paise to 95.68, and on Monday, it slumped 79 paise to 95.28. The rupee's depreciation is attributed to elevated crude prices and concerns over the West Asia crisis, weighing down the currency's value against the US dollar. The decline has been steady, with the rupee opening on a weak note and depreciating further in early trade on Thursday.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Slips Below $80,000, but 3 Warning Signs Flashed Red First Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 after a 37% rally stalled at the 200-day MA. Three warning signs flashed before the drop.
stories.summary: Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 after a 37% rally stalled at the 200-day moving average. The cryptocurrency's drop was preceded by three warning signs. The decline occurred after stronger-than-expected US producer price inflation data sparked a risk-off move, wiping out leveraged bullish bets. Bitcoin fell as much as 7.1% in Saturday afternoon trading in New York, marking its first drop below $80,000 since April 2025. This move exposed a more fragile market after weeks of gains. The drop was also influenced by global market reactions to President Donald Trump's Iran ceasefire warning and the latest US inflation data, which had previously caused Bitcoin to briefly dip below $80,000 on Tuesday. The cryptocurrency's price movement is being closely watched by options traders.

stories.headline: OpenAI proposes global AI watchdog with China ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: OpenAI has proposed a global AI watchdog, suggesting a governance body led by the US and including China. The proposal comes ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. OpenAI's VP, Chris Lehane, supports the creation of this global body to address AI safety, cybersecurity, and global competition. The upcoming summit in Beijing is expected to be a significant encounter between American and Chinese leaders, with discussions potentially focusing on these issues. The proposed global AI governance body aims to bring together major nations, including the US and China, to establish guidelines and regulations for the development and use of artificial intelligence. This move highlights the growing importance of AI in geopolitical discussions and the need for international cooperation to address related challenges.

stories.headline: Microsoft is shopping for artificial-intelligence startups as the software company prepares for a future independent of its once-vital partner OpenAI
stories.summary: Microsoft is shopping for artificial-intelligence startups to prepare for a future independent of its partner OpenAI. The software company aims to build a cutting-edge AI model by next year and is considering acquisitions to stock up on AI talent. This move comes as Microsoft and OpenAI's alliance is loosening, with both companies pursuing independent ambitions. Despite years of collaboration and over $13 billion in investment, Microsoft is looking to expand its AI capabilities without relying on OpenAI. The potential acquisitions will help Microsoft deliver on its goal of releasing a state-of-the-art AI model, according to sources familiar with the matter. This strategic move is part of Microsoft's efforts to stay competitive in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.

stories.headline: OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman holds more than $2 billion in companies that have done business with the artificial intelligence company
stories.summary: OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman holds over $2 billion in companies that have done business with the artificial intelligence company. This information was revealed in a court document, amid claims of self-dealing against Altman. State attorneys general, Elon Musk, and US lawmakers are scrutinizing Altman's investments, citing potential conflicts of interest. Altman has denied any wrongdoing, stating that he recused himself from key decisions involving the companies in which he has stakes. The revelation has led to intensified scrutiny, with a congressional investigation underway. Musk, who is suing OpenAI, has raised concerns about Altman's investments, seeking to highlight potential self-dealing practices. The issue has sparked legal and political questions, with Altman's leadership and business practices under examination.

stories.headline: OpenAI would support the creation of a global governance body for artificial intelligence led by the US and including China as a member, a top company executive
stories.summary: OpenAI supports the creation of a global governance body for artificial intelligence, led by the US and including China as a member. The company's endorsement comes as competition between the US and China intensifies. A top OpenAI executive expressed support for the proposal, which would establish a framework similar to the International Atomic Energy Agency. The global AI governance body would aim to regulate and oversee the development of artificial intelligence. By including China, the body would provide a platform for international cooperation and collaboration on AI issues. The proposal is seen as a significant development in the ongoing debate about the regulation of AI, with OpenAI's support adding weight to the idea of a US-led global governance body. The move is also notable given the timing, coming ahead of a high-stakes meeting between US and Chinese leaders.
